title: Checkmate at Midnight
letter:
Detective Knight,

My husband has summoned our household for an announcement tonight. Since then, he has dismissed his guards, accused old friends, and begun locking his study.

This evening, I found a note beneath his door:
“Before dawn, your reign ends.”

He calls it a childish threat. I fear he is wrong.
Please come to Blackrook Manor before midnight.

—Lady Scarlet

arrival.speaker: Scarlet
arrival.text: I asked you to prevent a murder.

arrival.speaker: Knight
arrival.text: Then help me prevent the next mistake.

choices.label: Examine the wound.
choices.response: Little blood surrounds the injury. The letter opener bears Ash’s crest.

choices.label: Examine the goblet.
choices.response: Pale residue with a sharp, bitter scent clings to the goblet beside the King’s normal medicine bottle. The drink needs to be compared with the household’s medicine and its dosage records.

suspects.name: Lady Scarlet
suspects.opening: I sent for you because I feared for his life. Now everyone looks at my torn shawl as though it answers every question.

choices.label: Explain the torn shawl.
choices.response: I argued with him. I had packed to leave, and he threatened to cut me off. I tore the shawl on a dining chair, not in his study. If you have already decided, why ask?

choices.label: Why were you leaving?
choices.response: Because I could no longer bear this house. My carriage was booked three days ago. Voss went into the study after dinner carrying a ledger. When I saw him later, he carried nothing.

suspects.name: Prince Ash
suspects.opening: He could make you feel small without ever leaving his chair.

choices.label: Explain the family-crested letter opener.
choices.response: It was my gift to him. Yes, I took the new will. He had removed me as heir. But anyone could have picked up that opener.

choices.label: What was the last thing your father said?
choices.response: He drank and said Mara had made his medicine bitter enough to kill him. I thought he was insulting her again. I wrote the note, Detective. I wanted to frighten him, not kill him.

suspects.name: Mara
suspects.opening: I found him. That is all. Why does everyone keep saying it like a confession?

choices.label: Explain your access to the medicine.
choices.response: I prepared his normal dose, as I do every night. The strong draught is missing. I do not know how. If I say another word you will turn that against me too.

choices.label: Describe exactly what you saw.
choices.response: He was on the floor. The opener was already in his chest. I ran to fetch her ladyship. The folding screen moved although the window was shut. And Voss borrowed my keys this afternoon—for a library cabinet, he said.

suspects.name: Captain Flint
suspects.opening: Nobody entered from outside. On that, I will stake my life.

choices.label: Why did you leave your post?
choices.response: Ash paid me to leave a side door unguarded. He said he needed to get a document out. If he returned through it, I would not have seen him. I should never have taken the money.

choices.label: What did you see when you returned?
choices.response: Voss, leaving the study corridor. He asked if the gates were locked. Strange question for a man who said he was going to bed. I hid that because it exposed my absence.

suspects.name: Chancellor Voss
suspects.opening: The estate papers are private, Detective. Surely grief does not abolish privacy.

choices.label: Who benefits from the King’s death?
choices.response: A wife preparing to leave. A son stripped of his inheritance. His letter opener bore Ash’s crest, and Scarlet’s shawl was torn. Must I explain what they mean?

choices.label: Show me the estate accounts.
choices.response: The ledger is in the study. Yes, estate funds went into my holdings, but His Majesty approved those transfers. My private papers have no bearing on his death. You are making a grave mistake.

clues.text: A thread caught on a nail in the chair moved here after dinner matches Scarlet’s shawl. The damaged rail offers an innocent explanation for the tear.
The hidden draft disinherits Ash. Motive is not proof of murder.

The register describes the concentrated draught’s pale residue and sharp, bitter scent, and warns that a large dose is fatal. That bottle is missing. Mara’s normal, harmless dose is recorded separately.
Flint’s signed duty book records an unguarded study corridor shortly before midnight. A delivery from the Chancellor’s office is logged in that interval; the recipient’s copy should be in the study.
A travel flask in Voss’s document case is labelled as concentrated sleeping draught. Pale residue with a sharp, bitter scent clings to its mouth. Compare it with the drink and the medicine register.
The surviving scrap records estate funds paid into Voss’s private holdings. Its page number is legible; the study ledger could establish which account it belongs to.
The estate ledger records a delivery signed by Voss shortly before midnight. Numbered leaves are missing from the transfers section; compare any surviving account records with these entries.
Pale residue with a sharp, bitter scent clings to the goblet beside the King’s normal medicine bottle. The drink needs to be compared with the household’s medicine and its dosage records.

low_bleeding.title: Little blood at the wound
low_bleeding.text: The visible injury may have occurred after the King collapsed. This is a clue, not a complete medical conclusion.

scarlet.title: The Scarlet Verdict
scarlet.text: You name Lady Scarlet. “I wrote for help,” she says. “Remember that when you tell them what happened here.” Flint escorts her away. At dawn, Voss burns the remaining accounts. Another red thread is still caught on the chair Scarlet used at dinner.
scarlet.epitaph: You found a motive. Someone else supplied the evidence.
scarlet.shot: Scarlet crosses the entrance threshold; cut to the snagged thread and Voss at the hearth.

ash.title: The Fallen Heir
ash.text: You name Prince Ash. He places his coronet on the dining table. “I wrote the threat. I wanted him to listen. Just once. I did not kill him.” Flint takes him away. The goblet remains in the study, holding the clue your accusation failed to explain.
ash.epitaph: The threat was his. The murder was not.
ash.shot: Hold on the abandoned coronet, then rack attention to the goblet.

mara.title: The Disposable Pawn
mara.text: You name Mara. “I prepared his medicine and found him,” she says. “That does not mean I killed him. You never asked who used me.” She leaves her key ring on her bed. Voss volunteers to give a statement against her.
mara.epitaph: The smallest piece carried the blame for the largest crime.
mara.shot: Empty servants’ room, key ring on white linen; bishop’s shadow falls across the doorway.

voss_free.title: The Bishop Walks Free
voss_free.text: You identify Voss, but your case leaves a crucial link unsupported. “You have described suspicions, Detective,” he replies. “You were called here for proof.” He leaves pending further investigation. Days later, a parcel reaches your office. Inside is a black bishop.
voss_free.epitaph: You named the killer. You could not hold him.
voss_free.shot: Open gates at dawn, followed by a bishop resting on the opened letter.

fire.title: The Burning Board
fire.text: You pursue Voss before securing the case. He burns the remaining accounts and knocks a candle stand into the library curtain. Flint forces his way in. You help evacuate the household while Voss escapes through the smoke. Everyone else is safe, but the gaps in your evidence remain. The surviving notes cannot yet prove the murder.
fire.epitaph: You brought everyone out except the truth.
fire.shot: Exterior entrance silhouette, safe household grouped outside, smoke at upper windows. No extra playable room.

checkmate.title: Checkmate
checkmate.text: You assemble the household in the study. Voss points to the wound and talks of a family quarrel. You set down the goblet, his flask and the dosage register. “The wound is where you wanted us to begin.” The draught links his flask to the fatal drink; the estate ledger corroborates his diverted funds. His access to the King is established in your case notes. The injury drew attention away from the drink. Flint takes the bishop into custody. “Did you know from the beginning?” Scarlet asks. “No,” you reply. “That is why I kept investigating.”
checkmate.epitaph: Checkmate. The truth survives until morning.
checkmate.shot: Household tableau in study; detective slides a miniature knight beside the bishop on the desk chessboard.
